title: Flowise OAuth2 credential routes -- T1552 three handlers look up credentials by id alone, two are whitelisted from auth entirely
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-70474 (GHSA-wch5-xp77-fxg4),
affecting Flowise's OAuth2 credential `authorize`/`callback`/`refresh`
routes.

All three handlers in `routes/oauth2/index.ts` query the `Credential`
table with `findOneBy({ id: credentialId })` -- no `workspaceId`
filter -- unlike the standard credential service elsewhere in the
same codebase, which correctly scopes by both `id` and `workspaceId`.
Two of the three (`callback`, `refresh`) are additionally listed in
`WHITELIST_URLS`, skipping authentication entirely. Combined, this
allows: (1) any authenticated user to initiate an OAuth2 authorize
flow against another workspace's credential, leaking its `client_id`
and `scope`; (2) an unauthenticated attacker who knows a credential
UUID to forge a callback using the credential's UUID as the `state`
parameter, injecting attacker-controlled tokens into that credential;
and (3) an unauthenticated attacker to refresh any credential's
tokens and receive a live `access_token` in the response.

Detection logic flags a request to `/api/v1/oauth2-credential/callback`
or `/api/v1/oauth2-credential/authorize/:id` /
`/api/v1/oauth2-credential/refresh/:id` where the credential id in
the path does not belong to the requesting session's own workspace
-- the exact cross-workspace lookup gap this advisory's three-vector
proof of concept confirms end-to-end.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (FlowiseAI, via
GHSA, citing the exact source lines for all three handlers, the
contrasting correctly-scoped service, and a full automated PoC
script exercising all three vectors), fixed in Flowise 3.1.3 (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
